claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, could you tell me:
1. How many children you have?
2. Their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello, yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 18 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can see you have an 18-year-old son named Alex who lives with you.

Since Alex is 18, his eligibility depends on whether he's in approved education or training. Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 if they're in approved education or training.

Could you tell me - is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as A-levels, vocational qualifications, or an approved training course)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and isn't studying anything right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I need to ask a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

You mentioned Alex finished school - when did he finish his education or training? Was it recently or some time ago?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He finished a few months back, just after he turned 18.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. One final question to complete my assessment:

Has Alex started any paid work, and if so, is he working 24 hours or more per week? Or has he started claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't started any paid work, and he's not claiming any benefits himself either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit can only continue if they are under 20 **and** in approved education or training. Since Alex is 18 and not currently in any approved education or training, the eligibility requirement is not met.

There is a provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks if a young person leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, but this only applies to 16 or 17 year olds. Unfortunately, as Alex is 18, this extension doesn't apply to him.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future - for example, if he decides to return to education or start an approved training course - you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit again at that point, as long as he remains under 20 years old.

Since Alex is over 16, not in approved education or training, and the special 20-week provision does not apply to him due to his age, you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
